claim.pdf_says: Printed page 546 (PDF page 576) ends with '... in which the object is specified in the RAISING phrase.' and then the footer '546   ©ISO/IEC 2023'. Printed page 547 (PDF page 577) OPENS with the paragraph 'An exception status indicator is a conceptual entity that exists for each function, method, or program for each exception condition and has two states, set or cleared. The initial state of all exception status indicators is cleared. ...'
claim.markdown_says: Line 24149, still inside the page-576 slice and BEFORE '' at line 24151: '546 �ISO/IEC 2023 An exception status indicator is a conceptual entity that exists for each function, method, or program for each exception condition and has two states, set or cleared. ...'. The page-577 slice then starts at its SECOND paragraph, 'In addition to exception status indicators, a last exception status exists for the entire run unit.'
claim.why_it_matters: The opening normative paragraph of 14.6.13.1.1 on page 577 - the definition of an exception status indicator, its two states, its initial cleared state and how TURN / PERFORM WHEN enable it - is attributed to the wrong page, so a page-cited lookup of page 577 misses it. The page-576 running footer has additionally been OCR'd into the body as literal text with a U+FFFD replacement character where '©' belongs, so the paragraph reads '546 �ISO/IEC 2023 An exception status indicator ...'.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed on both sides, and it survives every refutation route I tried. PDF side (rendered at 300dpi and read directly). Page 576 (printed 546) ends its body with the 14.6.13.1.1 opening paragraph 'An exception condition is either a condition associated with a specific exception status indicator or an exception object. ... in which the object is specified in the RAISING phrase.' followed only by the running footer '546 (c)ISO/IEC 2023' and the license line. Page 577 (printed 547) opens - first body line under the 'ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' header - with 'An exception status indicator is a conceptual entity that exists for each function, method, or program for each exception condition and has two states, set or cleared.' and its second paragraph is 'In addition to exception status indicators, a last exception status exists for the entire run unit.' The claim quotes both pages accurately. Markdown side (specs/ISO_COBOL.md). The anchor is at line 24113 and at line 24154. The 'An exception status indicator is a conceptual entity...' paragraph sits at line 24152 - inside the page-576 slice, before the page-577 anchor - exactly as claimed. The page-577 slice's first body paragraph is at line 24159, 'In addition to exception status indicators...', i.e. the printed page's SECOND paragraph. So one full normative paragraph is attributed to the wrong page. Not mere page-break furniture. I checked the obvious refutation - that footers are simply retained by convention at every page boundary - and it fails. 'ISO/IEC 2023' appears in a non-header position only 4 times in the entire file, and this is the only one welded into the middle of a normative sentence. Footers are otherwise stripped, so this is an OCR defect, not a formatting convention. The U+FFFD is real and verified at the byte level: the codepoint sequence at that position is 0x35 0x34 0x36 0x20 0xFFFD 0x49 0x53 0x4F ('546 ISO'), a replacement character standing where '©' belongs. Notably it is the ONLY U+FFFD in the whole file, which corroborates it as an isolated OCR failure rather than an encoding convention. (A naive read of the paragraph is also self-refuting as spec text: a sentence cannot legitimately begin '546 ?ISO/IEC 2023 An exception status indicator is...'.) Meaning is affected in the way that matters for this workflow. The prose is not lost - linear reading order is preserved - but the page attribution is wrong by one paragraph, so any page-576/577-scoped slice comparison or page-cited lookup of printed page 547 misses the definitional paragraph of an exception status indicator, and the page-576 slice gains a paragraph the printed page does not contain. Combined with the corrupted footer text inside a normative sentence, this is a genuine content discrepancy, correctly classified structural.
verdict.corrected_description: CONFIRMED as described, with one correction to the cited line numbers - the claim's line references are each off by 3. Accurate statement: in specs/ISO_COBOL.md the page-576 anchor is at line 24113 and the page-577 anchor at line 24154 (not 24151). The misplaced paragraph is at line 24152 (not 24149), reading '546 <U+FFFD>ISO/IEC 2023 An exception status indicator is a conceptual entity that exists for each function, method, or program for each exception condition and has two states, set or cleared. ...'; it lies inside the page-576 slice although the PDF prints it as the opening paragraph of printed page 547 / PDF page 577. The page-577 slice consequently begins at line 24159 with the printed page's second paragraph, 'In addition to exception status indicators, a last exception status exists for the entire run unit.' The substance of the claim - one normative paragraph of 14.6.13.1.1 attributed to the wrong page, plus the page-546 running footer OCR'd into the body of that paragraph with U+FFFD in place of '©' - is fully verified. Two supporting facts the claim did not state: footers are otherwise stripped throughout the document (only 4 non-header 'ISO/IEC 2023' occurrences exist file-wide, and this is the only one embedded mid-sentence), and this U+FFFD is the only replacement character in the entire file. Suggested fix: move line 24152 to just after the page-577 anchor and delete the leading '546 <U+FFFD>ISO/IEC 2023 ' footer fragment from it.
